subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
intro: These problems take two or three steps. You will decompose composite figures into known shapes, find the area of trapezoids, compute the volume of right prisms with $V=Bh$, and find the surface area of rectangular prisms. Watch your units: lengths are linear, areas are square units, and volumes are cubic units.

items.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides $b_1=12\text{ cm}$ and $b_2=8\text{ cm}$ and a height of $h=5\text{ cm}$. Find its area.
A figure shaped like a house outline is a $10\text{ m}$ by $6\text{ m}$ rectangle with a triangle of base $10\text{ m}$ and height $4\text{ m}$ sitting on top. Find the total area.

steps: Decompose the figure into a rectangle and a triangle.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism (box) measures $9\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$. Find its surface area.

steps: A rectangular prism has three pairs of matching faces. Use $SA=2(lw)+2(lh)+2(wh)$.

items.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base $6\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$. The prism is $10\text{ cm}$ long. Find its volume.

steps: Use $V=Bh$, where $B$ is the area of the triangular base and $h$ is the prism length.

items.prompt: An $8\text{ ft}$ by $8\text{ ft}$ square has a $3\text{ ft}$ by $2\text{ ft}$ rectangular hole cut out of it. Find the remaining area.

steps: Find the area of the whole square: $A=8\times 8=64\text{ ft}^2$.
Find the area of the hole: $A=3\times 2=6\text{ ft}^2$.
Subtract the hole from the square: $64-6=58\text{ ft}^2$.

items.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides $b_1=9\text{ in}$ and $b_2=5\text{ in}$ and a height of $h=6\text{ in}$. Find its area.
An L-shaped figure is made by joining a $7\text{ m}$ by $3\text{ m}$ rectangle and a $4\text{ m}$ by $2\text{ m}$ rectangle so they do not overlap. Find the total area.

steps: Decompose the L-shape into the two non-overlapping rectangles.

items.prompt: A cube has an edge length of $6\text{ cm}$. Find its surface area.

steps: A cube has $6$ identical square faces, so $SA=6s^2$.
Find the area of one face: $s^2=6^2=36\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A box-shaped fish tank measures $5\text{ ft}$ long, $2\text{ ft}$ wide, and $1.5\text{ ft}$ deep. What volume of water can it hold when full?

steps: The tank is a rectangular prism, so $V=lwh$.

items.prompt: A figure is a $14\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ rectangle with two identical triangles, each with base $14\text{ cm}$ and height $3\text{ cm}$, attached one on top and one on the bottom (forming a hexagon-like shape). Find the total area.

steps: Decompose into the rectangle plus the two triangles.

items.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base $8\text{ m}$ and height $4.5\text{ m}$. The prism is $7\text{ m}$ long. Find its volume.

steps: Use $V=Bh$, where $B$ is the area of the triangular base.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism gift box measures $12\text{ in}$ by $6\text{ in}$ by $4\text{ in}$. How much wrapping paper is needed to cover all of its faces (ignore overlap)?

steps: Wrapping paper covers the surface area: $SA=2(lw)+2(lh)+2(wh)$.

items.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides $b_1=15\text{ cm}$ and $b_2=7\text{ cm}$ and a height of $h=4\text{ cm}$. Find its area.
A garden plot is a $20\text{ m}$ by $12\text{ m}$ rectangle with a $5\text{ m}$ by $4\text{ m}$ rectangular shed standing in one corner. Find the area of the garden not covered by the shed.

steps: Find the area of the whole plot: $A=20\times 12=240\text{ m}^2$.
Find the area of the shed: $A=5\times 4=20\text{ m}^2$.
Subtract the shed from the plot: $240-20=220\text{ m}^2$.

items.prompt: A storage container is a rectangular prism $3\text{ m}$ long, $2\text{ m}$ wide, and $2.5\text{ m}$ tall. Find its volume.

steps: The container is a rectangular prism, so $V=lwh$.
